The ported implementation. Source of the separator state machine, the quote/substitute branch order and the std::endl detection through the scratch stringstream.
The oracle. 12 START_SECTIONs, 178 lines; every expected string in tests/sv_out_stream.rs is transcribed from its TEST_EQUAL literals. Registered and built upstream (executables.cmake:284).

Not ported here. Read for the three members SVOutStream depends on: QuotingMethod (line 39), quote (line 553) and substitute (line 484). Only these are reproduced; a general StringUtils port is separate work.
Not ported here. Read for toStr(float/double) and the precision mapping comment at lines 309-318 that fixes 6 fractional digits for float and 15 for double.

Not ported here as a module. appendNumeric is the algorithm reproduced by source_float_text (T = double) and source_f32_text (T = float), including the NaN/inf spellings, the T(1e-2)/T(1e4) scientific thresholds evaluated at the argument's own width, the shortest-round-trip scientific mantissa of that width, the '+' removal with retained zero padding and the keep-one-fractional-digit rule. The char buf[64] overflow path at lines 136-139, which falls through to std::to_string(double), is not reproduced: the port clamps fixed_digits at MAX_FIXED_DIGITS instead, and neither behaviour is reachable from the source's own call sites.

source_anchors.operation: the separator is emitted only when newline_ is false, and the first field on a line clears the flag instead of emitting one; this is the whole state machine the class exists for
operator<<(std::string) throws Exception::IllegalArgument for a '\n' anywhere in the field, with the message "argument must not contain newline characters"; '\r' is not tested for

branch order inside a field: modify_strings_ off writes verbatim, else a quoting method other than NONE calls StringUtils::quote, else the separator is replaced by replacement_; QuotingMethod::NONE therefore never reaches quote
operator<<(char) routes through StringUtils::toStr(c) into the string overload, so a single character is quoted like any other field and a '\n' character is rejected
std::endl is detected by applying the function pointer to the member stringstream ss_ and testing the result for "\n", because comparing against &std::endl does not work under libc++ on macOS 10.9

ss_ is only cleared inside the newline branch, so a manipulator writing anything else leaves ss_ polluted and every later std::endl fails the equality test - after one std::ends the newline flag is never set again
operator<<(Newline) sets newline_ and writes "\n" without flushing, which is the performance difference the header recommends it for

write() calls ostream::write directly and never touches newline_, so a raw chunk ending in a newline leaves the stream believing it is mid-line; the header comment 'use only on a line of its own!' is the warning about exactly this
the stream precision is set to numeric_limits<double>::digits10, which affects only the generic non-arithmetic operator<< because the arithmetic one converts through StringUtils::toStr
the filename constructor throws Exception::FileNotWritable naming the path when the ofstream does not open; the stream constructor cannot fail

writeValueOrNan switches modification off, writes nan_ ("nan"), inf_ ("inf") or "-" + inf_, and restores the previous state; the texts are the protected members, not the uppercase "NaN" appendNumeric produces
the class documentation states that nl or std::endl is required as the line delimiter and that a literal "\n" 'won't be accepted' - it is rejected by the newline check in the string overload

quote with QuotingMethod::ESCAPE substitutes backslashes before quote characters, an order that cannot be swapped without double-escaping; DOUBLE doubles the quote character; NONE only skips the substitution and still adds the surrounding quotes
substitute returns the string unchanged when the pattern is empty, so an empty separator silently disables separator replacement as well as emitting nothing between fields

scientific notation is selected for a nonzero magnitude at or above T(1e4) or below T(1e-2) - the comparison is in the template argument's own arithmetic, so 0.01f, which equals float(1e-2), takes the fixed branch while the same value promoted to double does not; zero always takes the fixed branch and therefore prints "0.0"
the scientific mantissa uses to_chars with no precision, the shortest decimal that round-trips, explicitly so libc++ and libstdc++ agree and reference files need no update
a scientific mantissa with no decimal point gains ".0", so 1e4 is written "1.0e04" rather than "1e04"
only the leading '+' is removed from the exponent; the printf-style two-digit zero padding is kept, so the exponent of 1e4 is "04"
trailing fractional zeros are trimmed but at least one digit after the point is kept, so 5.0 prints "5.0" and not "5"

NaN is written "NaN" in upper case for compatibility with the removed Karma formatter, while infinities are "inf"/"-inf" specifically so the keep-one-digit rule cannot turn them into the unreadable "inf.0"

appendToStr(float) instantiates appendNumeric with T = float and precision writtenDigits<float>() = 6, so both the threshold comparison and std::to_chars run at float width; sv_out_stream::source_f32_text is that instantiation and no f32 is promoted to f64 before formatting
toStr(double) passes writtenDigits<double>() = 15 as the to_chars fixed precision, which is digits after the decimal point, not significant digits; toStr(float) passes 6

" for writeValueOrNan. The upstream -1.23e45 assertion accepts three platform spellings; the pinned NumericFormatting produces the third, "-1.23e45", and this port reproduces that one. Transcribed C++ literals are tier-3 evidence: no C++ was built or executed and no C++ output was retained, so this is not a tier-1 differential. The numeric formatter beyond those literals (1.0e04, 1.0e-03, 0.0, -0.0, 5.0, NaN, 1.0e308, f32 0.333333) is independently derived (tier 4) from the appendNumeric algorithm read line by line. The resource ceilings, the empty/newline separator rejection, the carriage-return rejection, the non-ASCII separator and field cases and the error-variant choices are tier 4; no upstream fixture reaches them.
gaps: The source class derives from std::ostream, so a caller can cast to the base and write past the separator bookkeeping. This port does not reproduce the base class; write_raw is the single controlled escape hatch, as SVOutStream::write is upstream.

The generic non-arithmetic operator<< template streams a value through the ostream with the constructor's 15-digit precision applied. write_display uses Rust's Display, which has no precision setting, so a Display implementation rendering a float spells it Rust's way; write_number is the source-equivalent route for numbers.
The filename constructor has no upstream START_SECTION at all: the test only exercises the ostream constructor. The create/create_with_options tests are therefore tier 4.

StringUtils is not ported. QuotingMethod, quote and the toStr numeric conversion are reproduced here because SVOutStream cannot be ported without them; substitute is expressed as str::replace. A DATASTRUCTURES/StringUtils work package should take these over and this module should then defer to it.
appendToStrLowP (3 fractional digits, the low-precision variant) is not ported: SVOutStream only ever calls the full-precision conversion.

docs/doc-coverage.json was not rewritten: src/format/sv_out_stream.rs measures 100.0% (44/44) and check_doc_coverage.py reports an improvement, but recording the new floor with --write touches a file outside this package's scope.
